author: screenrant
title: LEGO Batman Game Revives Shelved Batgirl Film with Detailed In‑Game Homage
text:
The new LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight includes a mission that mirrors the cancelled Warner Bros. Batgirl movie, featuring Firefly's Halloween attack, Barbara Gordon's Burnside suit and references to every era of Batman media.
Warner Bros. famously scrapped its live‑action Batgirl film after production wrapped, turning the project into a tax write‑off despite a cast that included Leslie Grace as Barbara Gordon, Brendan Fraser as Firefly and Michael Keaton returning as Batman.
The cancellation, which has become a cautionary tale in Hollywood, left fans with only a handful of stills and concept art to imagine what might have been. Four years later the newly released LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight offers a surprisingly detailed homage to that lost movie, weaving key plot points and costume designs into its first playable Batgirl mission.
In the opening level, a Halloween party in Gotham is set ablaze by Fraser's Firefly, exactly the scenario that was slated for the cancelled film. Barbara Gordon dons a prototype Batgirl suit, rushes into the fray and teams up with Keaton's Batman to bring the pyromaniac down.
The mission's dialogue, setting and even the timing of the attack mirror the script details that leaked after the film's demise, making the LEGO sequence feel less like a generic side quest and more like a deliberate reenactment of the abandoned narrative. Beyond the initial tribute, the game unlocks Batgirl's distinctive Burnside outfit, the very costume that Grace's character was seen wearing on set.
This visual nod reinforces the connection between the digital world and the unrealized movie, giving players a rare glimpse of the aesthetic that never made it to cinemas. The developers have packed the entire title with references that span Batman's entire media history, from the campy 1960s television series and Tim Burton's gothic vision to Christopher Nolan's realistic saga, the recent DCEU outings, and even the Rocksteady Arkham games whose open‑world traversal and detective mechanics heavily influence LEGO Batman's design.
By stitching together elements from every era-including canceled projects like Batgirl-the game positions itself as a comprehensive celebration of the Dark Knight's legacy. Critics and fans alike have praised LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight as one of the most ambitious LEGO titles ever made. Its ability to honor both beloved and forgotten chapters of Batman lore while delivering accessible gameplay makes it stand out in a crowded market of licensed games.
The Batgirl homage, while a focal point of discussion, is just one facet of a broader tapestry that includes nods to classic comic moments, animated series, and the evolving portrayal of the Caped Crusader across decades. For anyone curious about the film that never saw the light of day, the game offers perhaps the closest experience to watching Batgirl's debut, wrapped in the playful, brick‑built world that LEGO fans have come to expect
